audit.whatIsWrong: Chart gave Ryze Level 1 and Level 6 and Irelia the two-item stage, against a 41.53% win rate and against the page's own whys[4] ('lane is still hers') and whys[6] ('you finally own the extended duel').
audit.why: Packet chart reads Skill / Irelia x5 / Ryze. The content whys[] already describe exactly that shape — only the win[] and phases[].side cells were wrong.
audit.corrected: Skill / Irelia / Irelia / Irelia / Irelia / Irelia / Ryze with ratings, matched pairs across both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why treated Level 6 as a Ryze spike.
audit.why: Vanguard's Edge (125/105/85s) leaves a blade wall that damages and slows anyone walking through it — with no dash on Ryze that cuts the retreat, so 6 is her spike. Realm Warp is a delayed group portal, not an escape. Ryze's real spike is Seraph's plus a second mana item.
audit.corrected: Level 6 rewritten as hers with the wall named; two-item stage is the flip.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page says in three places that Defiant Dance blocks or absorbs Ryze's empowered Q burst.
audit.why: Riot's text for Defiant Dance: 'She takes reduced physical damage during the charge.' Ryze deals magic damage, so her W does nothing against his rotation — the page tells the player to fear an interaction that does not exist, and to delay a trade that actually goes through. Flawless Duet is 16/14.5/13/11.5/10 at 850 range, Bladesurge is 10/9/8/7/6 and refreshes on Marked or killed targets while healing her, so anti-heal decides the attrition.
audit.corrected: Defiant Dance restated as physical-only damage reduction, real cooldowns given, Bladesurge's heal tied to Grievous Wounds.

audit.whatIsWrong: Flawless Duet is the tracked cooldown but its number never appears.
audit.why: 16 seconds at rank 1 dropping to 10 at rank 5 is the window the whole page hangs on.
audit.corrected: Number added to the do-line, the interactions line and phases[1].why.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer calls Irelia 'he' and 'his' while the content layer uses 'she'.
audit.corrected: Pronouns fixed in the lines I touched.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 are pure survival — Irelia's passive stacks and Defiant Dance (W) block make your burst burst-resistant, and her Q resets mean she can kite your W root by dashing off your hitbox before the root connects. At level 6 she adds Vanguard's Edge (R), which creates a blade ring that slows and stuns anyone caught inside it — never step into it deliberately, and Flash away if she ults in your direction. Your job is to CS, avoid the stun, call for jungle pressure with your W root as reliable setup, and stall until first item.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 are pure survival — Irelia's passive stacks make her autos brutal, and her Q resets mean she can kite your W root by dashing off your hitbox before the root connects. Defiant Dance does not help her here: it reduces physical damage, so your magic rotation lands in full. At level 6 she adds Vanguard's Edge, whose blade wall damages and slows anyone walking through it — with no dash, hold Flash for that wall rather than for the damage. CS, avoid the stun, call jungle pressure off your root, and stall to first item.

notes: The serious error: the page says three times that Defiant Dance blocks or absorbs Ryze's empowered Q. Riot's own text says she takes reduced PHYSICAL damage during the charge — Ryze deals magic, so her W is irrelevant to his burst and the player was being told to wait out a window that does not exist. No mirror audit existed for this matchup, so the chart is aligned to the packet and to the content whys[], which already described an Irelia-favoured lane. Note phases[5]/win[5] stay Irelia per the packet even though whys[5] calls first item 'your first genuine fighting window' — I read that as the first stage you can trade back in, not a stage you own, and left it.
